messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Multi-turn spiral
parts:
Consider 

     spiral <- data.frame(t=0:99,r=0:99)

I would like to plot this as a four-turn spiral, that is, consider that a full turn of the circle is defined as t=0..25.  Put differently, use theta=(t %%25)*2*pi.

I don't see how to do this straightforwardly with something like

      ggplot(spiral) + geom_line(aes(x=t,y=r)) + coord_polar()

because coord_polar always assumes that a full turn is equal to the range of x.

A workaround is to split the spiral into 'turns', like this:

      ggplot(spiral) + geom_line(aes(x=t %%25,y=r,group=t %/% 25)) + coord_polar()

but unfortunately that gives discontinuities at t %% 25 == 0.

The simplest solution, I think, would be to have a parameter to coord_polar which defined the wraparound point (and also a parameter saying whether to connect the last point to the first).

Is there anything like this available?

The above is a simplified example.  My actual application is to look at density plots of daily Web site usage which varies by day of week.

One way to do that is with facet_grid or with groups:

      ggplot(df) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) + facet_grid(day ~ .)
      ggplot(df) + geom_density(aes(x=x,group=day,colour=day))

But in both these cases, the day-breaks are arbitrary.  If I'm getting a lot of traffic from Australia, it will be split across two days both visually and (worse) by the density calculation.

One solution to this is to work with extended days, where each day includes parts of the adjoining days.

Another solution would be to use a polar plot, with each turn of the circle being one day; so there would be 7 lines.  This still has a discontinuity at the end of the week (in both the density calculation and the line plotting), but that is better than having it at the end of each day.

Of course, even better would be to have ggplot itself 'understand' periodic data, and use more appropriate density and interpolation algorithms.

             -s

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: Multi-turn spiral
parts:
Hi, is this still the state of multi-turn polar graphs in ggplot2?  Stavros's code produces the same described interruption, but I was curious if there's a new approach since September.  I wrote the attached graph with base graphics, and I'd like to rewrite it in ggplot2 before exposing it in a package.


I was hoping that setting theta's limits (through scale_x_continuous()) would force the multiple turns, but it seems just to drop everything beyond the upper limit of theta.  For instance, this is a slight adaptation of a panel in Fig 7.11 in the UseR book.
line <- data.frame(x = c(1, 200), y = c(100, 1))
base <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x, y)) + geom_line(data = line)
base <- base + coord_polar("x") 
#This works:
base + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0, 200))
#This doesn't work (presumably because 50 < 200)
#base + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0, 50))

Regarding a workaround, Stavros, did you consider interpolating the interruption?  Kinda like the colors were interpolated in the top graph on page 54.  It might have to be done twice for each interruption.
